He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona Gaels]] and the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. With Florida, Clayton was a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in 2025 and was named the [[NCAA Division I basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] (MOP) after leading Florida to a [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship]] victory. ==Early life and high school career== Clayton was born in [[Sebring, Florida]], on March 6, 2003. He is the son of Cherie Ann Quarg, who played [[softball]] and basketball at Frostproof Middle-Senior High School{{cite book |last=Quarg |first=Cherie |title=Remember When ... |date=2002 |publisher=Frostproof Middle Senior High School |edition=54 |location=Frostproof, Florida |page=139}} and Walter Clayton Sr., who played basketball and [[American football|football]] at Frostproof.{{cite web |last=Burack |first=Emily |date=April 4, 2025 |title=Get to Know Walter Clayton Jr.'s Family |url=https://townandcountrymag.com/leisure/sporting/a64300932/walter-clayton-jr-family-tree-parents-daughter-girlfriend-facts/ |access-date=April 8, 2025 |website=Town & Country |publisher=Hearst Digital Media}} His family moved to [[Lake Wales, Florida]], when he was 10.{{cite web |last=Harry |first=Chris |title=Coming Home: From Gael Force to Gator |url=https://floridagators.com/news/2023/7/18/coming-home-from-gael-force-to-gator-walter-clayton-jr-july-18-2023.aspx |access-date=March 30, 2025 |website=Florida Gators |date=July 18, 2023}} Clayton Jr. initially attended [[Lake Wales High School]], where he played football and basketball.{{cite web |last=Fuoco |first=Roy |date=April 3, 2021 |title=Bartow's Walter Clayton put in hard work to become complete player |url=https://www.theledger.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2021/04/03/hard-work-pushed-bartows-clayton-becoming-complete-player/4848122001/ |access-date=March 21, 2023 |website=[[The Ledger]]}} In basketball, he averaged 17.5 points, five rebounds, and 3.2 assists as a sophomore.{{cite web |last=Fuoco |first=Roy |date=November 24, 2019 |title=Clayton tops Elite 8 list for boys basketball |url=https://www.theledger.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2019/11/24/clayton-tops-elite-8-list-for-boys-basketball/2221239007/ |access-date=March 22, 2023 |website=[[The Ledger]]}} Clayton transferred to [[Bartow High School]] after his sophomore year.{{cite web |last=Fuoco |first=Roy |date=August 16, 2019 |title=Two-sport star Clayton transfers from Lake Wales to Bartow |url=https://www.theledger.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2019/08/16/two-sport-star-clayton-transfers-from-lake-wales-to-bartow/4447185007/ |access-date=March 21, 2023 |website=[[The Ledger]]}} He averaged 15.4 points, 4.3 assists, 4.3 rebounds, and 2.3 steals per game during his first season at Bartow as the Yellow Jackets won the Florida Class 6A state championship.{{cite web |last=Fuoco |first=Roy |date=March 21, 2020 |title=All-County: Clayton's focus on basketball paid off big |url=https://www.theledger.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2020/03/21/all-county-claytons-focus-on-basketball-paid-off-big/1480647007/ |access-date=March 22, 2023 |website=[[The Ledger]]}} Clayton committed to playing college basketball for [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]] over offers from [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]], [[Florida A&M Rattlers basketball|Florida A&M]], [[Charleston Cougars men's basketball|Charleston]], [[Stetson Hatters men's basketball|Stetson]], and [[James Madison Dukes men's basketball|James Madison]].{{cite web |last=Fuoco |first=Roy |date=November 17, 2020 |title=Bartow's Clayton signs with Iona |url=https://www.theledger.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2020/11/17/bartows-clayton-signs-iona/6322300002/ |access-date=March 22, 2023 |website=[[The Ledger]]}} Clayton was considered a better college prospect in football and began playing the sport as a freshman in high school at the urging of his childhood friend, [[Gervon Dexter]].{{cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |date=March 15, 2023 |title=Walter Clayton Jr. traded football for basketball and it's paying off |url=https://nypost.com/2023/03/15/walter-clayton-jr-traded-football-for-basketball-ahead-ncaa-tournament/ |access-date=March 21, 2023 |website=[[New York Post]]}} He had offers to play football from [[Florida Gators football|Florida]], [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]], [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], and [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia]].{{cite web |last=Singer |first=Mike |date=June 23, 2019 |title=2021 Florida ATH Walter Clayton Is The "Total Package" |url=https://tennessee.rivals.com/news/2021-florida-ath-walter-clayton-is-the-total-package-?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAANCjgVS8fj13eRpbd_zJkpX1-o0BHj0zHRB01zfo7k8uaFQPQbsvcfn5NK3Prrj6MbAzQaEX04CsEVOoEUzRsDRgTTpOk-8QpAxF93vjZYwIXsWRjE_EBekhX-w16c27Hhv5_1WWFhTbLdH-lbA_sKgkWwX2wPZ1Kfp8xmaCjj1F |access-date=March 22, 2023 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}} ==College career== === Iona (2021–2023) === Clayton averaged 7.3 points per game during his freshman season at Iona. He was named the [[Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference (MAAC) Player of the Year]] as a sophomore after averaging 16.8 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 3.2 assists per game during the regular season.{{cite web |last=Rapay |first=Eugene |date=March 8, 2023 |title=Iona men's, women's basketball stars, coaches win 2022–23 MAAC awards |url=https://www.lohud.com/story/sports/college/iona/2023/03/08/iona-gaels-mens-womens-basketball-stars-coaches-win-maac-awards/69985768007/ |access-date=March 21, 2023 |website=[[The Journal News]]}} After the season, Clayton entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web |date=March 22, 2023 |title=Reports: MAAC POY Walter Clayton Jr. to transfer from Iona |url=https://www.mdjonline.com/fieldlevel/reports-maac-poy-walter-clayton-jr-to-transfer-from-iona/article_233f1ff6-943b-54ae-864a-51109eaaec24.html |access-date=March 22, 2023 |website=[[Marietta Daily Journal]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} === Florida (2023–2025) === Clayton ultimately transferred to the Florida [[Florida Gators|Gators]].{{cite web |last=Bass |first=Tobias |last2=Moore |first2=CJ |last3=Vecenie |first3=Sam |date=April 11, 2023 |title=Walter Clayton Jr. transfers to Florida: How former Iona guard fits with Gators |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4401388/2023/04/11/walter-clayton-jr-florida-transfer-iona/ |access-date=April 11, 2023 |website=[[The Athletic]]}} He also had considered transferring to [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] and playing for his former Iona head coach, [[Rick Pitino]].{{cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |date=March 23, 2023 |title=Iona star Walter Clayton choosing between St. John's and Florida |url=https://nypost.com/2023/03/23/iona-star-walter-clayton-choosing-between-st-johns-and-florida/ |access-date=April 11, 2023 |website=[[New York Post]]}} In his first season at Florida, Clayton averaged 17.6 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 2.6 assists and was honored as Second-Team All-SEC.{{cite web |title=Walter Clayton Jr. College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/walter-claytonjr-1.html |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=Sports-Reference.com}} He played an instrumental role in getting the Gators to the SEC Tournament Championship for the first time in 10 years and the NCAA Tournament for the first time in 3 years.{{cite web |date=March 16, 2025 |title=No. 4 Florida Gators win 1st SEC Tourney title since 2014 after beating No. 8 Tennessee 86-77 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/mens-college-basketball/news/no-4-florida-gators-win-1st-sec-tourney-title-since-2014-after-beating-no-8-tennessee-86-77 |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=NBC Sports |agency=Associated Press}} Despite the loss, Clayton had 33 points in a historic performance against Colorado in the 2024 NCAA Tournament.{{cite web |last=Solomon |first=Bennett |date=March 22, 2024 |title=Gators lose in heartbreaking fashion, fall to Colorado in Round of 64 |url=https://www.alligator.org/article/2024/03/gators-lose-in-heartbreaking-fashion-fall-to-colorado-in-round-of-64?ct=content_open&cv=cbox_latest |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=The Independent Florida Alligator}} After the [[2023–24 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2023–24 season]], Clayton declared for the [[2024 NBA Draft|NBA Draft]].{{cite web |last=Dubbin |first=Adam |date=April 8, 2024 |title=Gators star guard declares for NBA draft, might return to Florida |url=https://gatorswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/gators/mens-basketball/2024/04/08/florida-basketball-walter-clayton-declares-for-nba-draft-couldreturn-to-gators/73250002007/ |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=Gators Wire |publisher=USA Today}} However, he ended up withdrawing from the draft and returning to Florida for his senior season.{{cite web |last=Bernstein |first=Max |date=May 27, 2024 |title=Guard Walter Clayton Jr. withdraws from draft, will return to Florida |url=https://www.alligator.org/article/2024/05/guard-walter-clayton-jr-withdraws-from-draft-will-return-to-florida?ct=content_open&cv=cbox_latest |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=The Independent Florida Alligator}} It was during this season that Clayton had one of the best individual seasons in Florida basketball history. He led [[2024-25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] to a 27–4 record in the regular season while averaging 17.2 points, 4.3 assists, and 3.8 rebounds. During this season, Clayton led Florida to wins over [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|No. 1 Tennessee]] and at [[2024–25 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|No. 1 Auburn]], which was the first time Florida had ever beaten a No. 1 on the road.{{cite web |date=January 7, 2025 |title=Gators Dismantle No. 1 Vols in Historic Blowout |url=https://floridagators.com/news/2025/1/7/mens-basketball-gators-dismantle-no-1-tennessee-in-historic-blowout-jan-7-2025.aspx |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=Florida Gator Athletics}}{{cite web |date=April 11, 2025 |title=No. 6 Florida beats top-ranked Auburn 90-81 and ends the Tigers' 14-game winning streak |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401708375 |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} He also helped lead Florida to its best overall record and SEC record in 11 years. After the regular season, Clayton was honored as first-team All-SEC selection.{{cite web |last=Dubbin |first=Adam |date=March 12, 2025 |title=Florida Gators Walter Clayton Jr, Alex Condon earn All-SEC Team honors |url=https://gatorswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/gators/mens-basketball/2025/03/12/florida-basketball-all-sec-team-walter-clayton-jr-alex-condon/82310747007/ |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=Gators Wire |publisher=USA Today}} On March 18, 2025, Clayton was named a first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All American]].{{cite web |last=Rosenberg |first=David |date=March 18, 2025 |title=Florida basketball G Walter Clayton Jr. named AP First Team All-American |url=https://gatorswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/gators/mens-basketball/2025/03/18/florida-gators-basketball-walter-clayton-ap-all-america-first-team/82523267007/ |access-date=March 26, 2025 |website=Gators Wire |publisher=USA Today}} Clayton went on to lead the Gators to the national championship, making a crucial defensive closeout, causing Houston's [[Emanuel Sharp]] to pump-fake on a potential game-winning three-pointer and lose his dribble.{{cite web |date=April 8, 2025 |title=Walter Clayton Jr.'s defensive stop gives Florida its 3rd national title with 65–63 win over Houston |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/walter-clayton-jr-s-defensive-stop-gives-florida-its-3rd-national-title-with-65-63-win-over-houston/ |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=CBSSports.com}} Clayton's teammate [[Alex Condon]] pounced on the loose ball to seal the Gators' third national championship in program history and first since 2007.{{cite web |last=Spits |first=Scott |date=April 8, 2025 |title=Australian basketballer Alex Condon helps Florida Gators NCAA 2025 basketball title |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/former-ruckman-nabs-biggest-title-in-us-college-basketball-with-desperate-final-act-20250408-p5lq6b.html |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=The Sydney Morning Herald}}{{cite web |date=April 8, 2025 |title=Florida downs Houston in thriller, captures first title since 2007 |url=https://www.ncaa.com/live-updates/basketball-men/d1/florida-downs-houston-thriller-captures-first-title-2007 |access-date=April 11, 2025 |website=NCAA.com}} Clayton was named the [[NCAA Division I basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] (MOP).{{cite web |last=Young |first=Ryan |title=NCAA championship: Florida's Walter Clayton Jr. wins Final Four Most Outstanding Player after leading Gators past Houston |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/college-basketball/article/ncaa-championship-floridas-walter-clayton-jr-wins-final-four-most-outstanding-player-after-leading-gators-past-houston-032428882.html |access-date=April 7, 2025 |website=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |date=April 7, 2025}} After the season, Clayton was named the [[SEC Male Athlete of the Year]], making him the first Florida basketball player to receive this honor. ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2025–2026)=== On June 25, 2025, Clayton was selected with the 18th overall pick by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the first round of the [[2025 NBA draft]] and subsequently traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] for the draft rights to [[Jamir Watkins]] and [[Will Riley]].{{cite web |last1=Koch |first1=Jared |title=Utah Jazz Trade Up to Select Walter Clayton Jr. |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/onsi/news/utah-jazz-trade-up-select-walter-clayton-jr-nba-draft |website=SI.com |access-date=February 23, 2026 |date=June 25, 2025}} On July 2, Clayton signed with the Jazz alongside [[Ace Bailey (basketball)|Ace Bailey]].{{cite web |title=Utah Jazz Sign Ace Bailey and Walter Clayton Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-ace-bailey-and-walter-clayton-jr |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 23, 2026 |date=July 2, 2025}} On October 22, Clayton made his NBA debut with the Jazz, recording ten points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals in a 129–108 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web |title=Kessler scores 22 points to lead Jazz past Clippers 129-108 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022500087 |access-date=August 25, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} On December 7, he scored a career-high 20 points, alongside nine assists, in a 131–101 loss against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |title=Thunder improve to 23-1 with 15th straight victory, routing Jazz 131-101 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022500363 |access-date=August 25, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} Clayton made 45 appearances for Utah during the 2025–26 season, averaging 6.8 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 5.5 assists. ===Memphis Grizzlies (2026–present)=== On February 3, 2026, Clayton, [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]], [[Taylor Hendricks]], [[Georges Niang]], and three first-round draft picks were traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Jaren Jackson Jr.]], [[John Konchar]], [[Jock Landale]], and [[Vince Williams Jr.]]{{cite web |title=Grizzlies acquire Walter Clayton Jr., Taylor Hendricks, Kyle Anderson, Georges Niang and Three Future First Round Draft Picks from Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-walter-clayton-jr-taylor-hendricks-kyle-anderson-georges-niang-and-three-future-first-round-draft-picks-from-jazz | access-date=February 4, 2026 |website=NBA.com |date=February 3, 2026}} On February 6, Clayton made his debut with the Grizzlies, scoring 11 points, and tallying up three rebounds, four assists, and a steal in a 135–115 loss against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. On April 5, he matched his career-high of 20 points, alongside three rebounds and four assists, in a 131–115 loss against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |title=Bucks outlast Grizzlies 131-115 in battle of short-handed teams |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022501135 |access-date=August 25, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} ==Personal life== Clayton and his girlfriend, Tatiyana Burney, had a daughter in December 2023.{{cite web |last=Marks |first=Brendan |date=April 8, 2025 |title=Walter Clayton Jr.'s fairytale Florida journey gets fitting national championship ending |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6263626/2025/04/08/walter-clayton-jr-florida-national-championship/ |access-date=April 8, 2025 |website=The Athletic}}{{cite web |last=Mader |first=Daniel
